== Course of events ==

Having discovered a tiny golden key upon a glass table and found all the doors in the hall locked, Alice comes upon a fan. When she takes it up and uses it, she discovers to her alarm that it causes her to shrink most rapidly. In her distress at vanishing away to nothing, she drops the fan to prevent her complete disappearance, and finds herself standing at only two feet in height. Shortly after, her form undergoes a most startling reversal, and Alice grows to nine feet tall. Her body becomes disproportionately large—a change of such peculiar and unsettling proportions that it causes her considerable distress, particularly regarding her feet, which are now at such a distance from her head that she can scarce manage them.

This extraordinary alteration of her size proves to be but one in a series of transformations that mark her journey through Wonderland. Having grown so tall, she later comes to realize with some astonishment that she is swimming in a pool of her own tears—the very tears she had shed when she was nine feet tall. The experience leaves her in a state of bewilderment regarding her own identity, causing her to wonder whether she has become someone altogether different, and she finds herself comparing her present state to children she once knew, such as Ada and Mabel. When the White Rabbit appears, dressed in his formal attire, he takes one look at her and flees in terror, dropping his gloves and fan as he goes.
